title: Shared decoder plus per-function Mirror codes versus ordinary latent codes
hypothesis: Across 16 continuous functions, a shared MLP decoder with two per-function Givens angles achieves held-out query normalized RMSE within 10% of a two-dimensional ordinary latent code while using <=80% its actual serialized bytes.
mirror_coordinate: two per-function Givens angles applied to hidden feature pairs
logical_multiplicity: 16 distinct continuous functions decoded by one shared network
controls: ordinary latent code dimensions 1, 2, and 8 concatenated to decoder input

task.teacher: random weighted Fourier sums with frequencies 1, 2, 3

success_gate: Mirror normalized RMSE is <=1.1x latent2 RMSE on each fresh world and Mirror payload <=80% latent2 payload; report all other code dimensions and independent upper control.
failure_gate: Mirror misses either the quality or actual-byte gate, or latent2 weakly dominates it.
boundaries: Synthetic 1D functions only; not DeepSDF/3D evidence.
Fresh worlds use new functions and query samples.
Fixed-update results are not near-converged capacity claims.
